study type: Case series and in vitro experimental study
cohort: The study included two patients with Hyaline Fibromatosis Syndrome (HFS) and deleterious ANTXR2 mutations experiencing congenital diarrhea and severe protein-losing enteropathy, alongside patient-derived and CRISPR-Cas9 ANTXR2 knockout intestinal organoids compared to organoids from two healthy controls.
finding: Loss of ANTXR2-mediated signaling in patients with Hyaline Fibromatosis Syndrome leads to collagen VI accumulation in the duodenum and abnormal extracellular matrix composition, which likely plays a role in the development of protein-losing enteropathy, despite intact epithelial cell function.
